slides.texte_overlay:
Breathing tricks that
calm you down in seconds
The long exhale. Breathe in for four seconds, out for six. A longer exhale tells your body it's safe and slows your heart.
The double inhale. Two short breaths in through the nose, then one long breath out. It's one of the fastest ways to calm a stressed body.
Box breathing. Four seconds in, hold four, out four, hold four. Repeat for a minute before a meeting or a hard conversation.
Breathe through your nose. Mouth breathing keeps you in alarm mode. Nose breathing is slower and calmer all day long.
Before: stress took over my evenings. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a few slow breaths, and my head is calmer.

slides.texte_overlay: Breathe low, not high. Put a hand on your belly and feel it rise. Chest breathing is tense, belly breathing is relaxed.
Practise when you're calm. Two minutes a day trains the habit, so it works automatically when stress hits. Practise daily.
